outputs.explanation: The scatter plot itself plots all n=141 individual samples as points (no averaging), and the accompanying marginal histograms show the actual binned counts of these individual measurements (with a fitted gamma curve overlaid), so individual data are directly visible rather than hidden behind a summary statistic.

Each point represents the mean ± s.d. across 6 replicate samples per reporter/cell line (n=2 biological x triplicate/duplicate technical replicates). Only the averaged value and its error bar are shown; the individual replicate measurements that went into each mean are not plotted.

The panel shows fitted normal-distribution curves of subtype-averaged periods and amplitudes, built from already-averaged per-cell-line values (n=1–4 cell line models per subtype, themselves averages of 3–6 replicates). No individual cell-line data points (e.g., as dots or a histogram of the underlying averaged values) are overlaid on the smooth curves, so the spread of the small number of contributing values is hidden.

The boxplots have individual sample data points (purple for Per2-Luc, pink for Bmal1-Luc) overlaid on top of the boxes for each cell line, so the underlying n=4–12 individual ridge-length measurements are directly visible alongside the summary boxplot statistics.

These are polar histograms showing the full distribution (binned by probability) of phase-difference values over time for each cell line; a histogram inherently displays the underlying data distribution rather than collapsing it to a single mean with error bar, so no additional individual-point overlay is required.

Like panel E, this is a polar histogram depicting the distribution of subtype-level phase-difference values across time (with per-cell-line breakdowns already provided in panel E). As a histogram-type distribution plot rather than a single mean-with-error summary, it does not require separate individual point markers.

This panel is an illustrative example of a single fitted signal (original trace, fitted sinusoid, and decay envelope) used to explain the fitting method; it is not a summary/average across replicates, so individual-data-point display is not applicable.

Each of the n=117 points plotted is an individual sample's fitted amplitude and decay rate; the error bars represent the fitting uncertainty (s.d.) of that individual sample's parameters, not an average across multiple replicate samples, so individual data are already shown directly.
